title: Start: the NEAT brief, deadline Friday 17:00
text: BRIEF.md in this folder was a stale copy of the lunarlander-98 brief, a project already finished (PPO 98.8% / 98.4%). The user confirmed the real brief is NEXT_PROJECT_BRIEF.md: NEAT from a clean start, a curriculum, a network sized by measurement, a fast C++ simulator for training, and boulder layout v3. Deadline Friday 2026-11-06 17:00, wrap-up from 16:27. Machine: i5-8250U, 4 cores / 8 threads, 7.6 GB, no usable GPU.

title: Boulder layout v3 in the frozen task
text: One approved change to the world: the boulder's bottom now stays at least 3.5 m above the pad (v2: 1.73 m, less than the lander's 1.8 m height). Same random stream as v2, so each seed keeps its boulder size and sideways position; only the height moved, into a 3.0 m band. Test: on 100,000 seeds of each of the 6 seed ranges, every clearance holds. The passability test (a planner that may read the true wind, used only as a test) comes next.

title: How big must the network be? Copies say: more than 16 hidden nodes
text: The PPO champion (16->128->128->4) was copied by imitation (DAgger, the same budget each) into small networks and each copy flew the same 1,000 fresh analysis flights of layout v3. 16->8->4: 56.5%. 16->16->4: 79.1%. 16->32->4: 87.0%. The PPO original: 98.9% (its first number on v3; failures: 10 boulder touches, 1 crash). So small networks are not enough. The copies are only a yardstick: NEAT starts from random genomes. The test was stopped before the bigger sizes when the user asked to go straight to NEAT.

title: Run N1 starts: NEAT from random genomes, goal 95%
text: The user's decision today: NEAT from scratch with a curriculum, a population big enough to evolve, nodes that can be added and removed; stop at 95% or Friday 17:00 (the brief's 98% is lowered to 95%). Set-up: population 300, every genome 16 inputs -> 32 random tanh hidden nodes -> 4 outputs (640 connections), weights random; mutation nudges 80% of weights by N(0, 0.1), adds nodes (3%) and connections (5%), deletes nodes (2%) and connections (2%). Speciation retuned every generation to keep ~12 species. All genomes of a generation fly the same seeds; the top 10 re-fly 40 selection seeds. Curriculum N1: calm landing with fading training wheels -> wind ramp 5->15 with turbulence -> boulder growing 0.4->1.0 with 40% real-task rehearsal -> real task with 30% hard cases. Speed in the Python reference simulator: ~40,000-50,000 steps/s on 7 workers, ~20 s per calm generation; the C++ simulator is postponed until speed is the bottleneck. Expectation written before the result: >= 90% calm landings within ~250 generations.

title: Bug found: the species threshold ran away (0.25 -> 35)
text: Check-in at gen 54. Calm landing is learned: the champion lands 100% of its calm training flights since gen 18 (training wheels still 0.82 -> 0.46), mean fitness -342 -> +179. But my speciation controller is broken: it raises the compatibility threshold 10% per generation whenever there are more than 12 species, and the count has been stuck at 14 since gen 3 while the threshold went 0.25 -> 35. neat-python keeps old species as long as genomes stay within the threshold of their representative, so the count never responded. With a threshold of 35 no new species can form; as stagnant species are removed, the population would collapse into one species and new structure would lose its protection. Change (one): clamp the threshold to 0.15-1.0 and step it 5% per generation; reset it to 0.5 at the restart. Expectation before the result: the species count should drift towards ~12, and calm-landing progress should not suffer.

title: Stage 1 passed; species down to 3, so the threshold floor goes 0.15 -> 0.05
text: Stage 1 (calm landing) passed at gen 100: the champion landed 96.5% of 200 fresh calm flights with no training wheels, confirmed at 97.5% on another fresh 200. Stage 2 (wind ramp) started; at gen 151 the push is 7.5 (75% steady) and the champion still lands all its training flights; the real task is at 6% (best so far). Problem: species fell from 13 to 3 (exactly 100 genomes each) with the threshold stuck at its floor 0.15. Measured on the gen-150 checkpoint: genomes are a median 0.94 apart, but each species is one tight lineage whose members are within 0.15 of each other, so no new species can split off while stagnation removes old ones down to the 3 protected by species_elitism. Change (one): lower the threshold floor to 0.05 so the controller can split lineages again (target ~12). Expectation before the result: species back to 8-12 within ~30 generations, no drop in the champion's landing rate.

title: The champion's network is now saved at every check
text: For The model tab (the user asked to see the network and how it develops): the trainer now saves the generation champion's network every 10 generations (runs/N1/champions/*_track.json). No change to evolution itself. Restarted from the checkpoint.

title: Correction: species collapsed because of a resume bug, not the threshold floor
text: At the 16:45 check-in I blamed the species collapse (13 -> 3) on the threshold floor of 0.15 and lowered it to 0.05. That was wrong: species stayed at 3. Measured on the gen-195 checkpoint: members sit 0.37-0.48 from their representative, which is impossible with a threshold of 0.05. Cause: when the run resumes, the species set comes back from the pickle with its own copy of the settings, so speciation kept the threshold it had at the first restart (gen 57): 46.8, the runaway value. Since gen 57 every genome was lumped into an existing species and stagnation removed them down to the 3 protected by species_elitism; my controller was tuning a number nobody read. Fix: on resume, the species set and the trainer share one settings object, and a test checks it. Expectation before the result: new species form within a few generations (threshold restarts at 0.3), heading for ~12.

title: Crash after the species fix; threshold set by measurement
text: After the resume fix, the threshold I restarted with (0.3) split the population into 105 species, and neat-python stopped with an error (105 species x 3 genomes minimum > 300 genomes). The supervisor restarted it twice from the gen-196 checkpoint with the same result; no generations were lost beyond these retries. This time I chose the threshold by simulation on the saved population: 0.3 -> 79 species, 0.4 -> 13, 0.45 -> 6, 0.5 and above -> 3. Set to 0.4. Guard added so this cannot stop the run again: when there are very many species, the per-species minimum and elitism shrink for that generation and the threshold rises 30% per generation instead of 5%.

title: Wind ramp review: paced ramps, early pass, boulder practice, automatic end
text: Diagnosis (200 analysis flights each): the gen-211 champion landed 97.5% in its current training world, 67% in full wind without a boulder (gen 100: 15.5%), 0% in calm air with a boulder (73% boulder hits), 1% on the real task. So wind learning works; the low real-task line is the boulder, which the curriculum had not trained yet, and the fixed-clock ramp was slow while the champion landed 97-100% of its flights. Changes at gen 230: (1) ramps are paced: 3 steps per generation while the champion lands >= 90% of its own flights in the current world, 1 at >= 70%, 0.5 below; (2) the stage's final world is checked every 10 generations from the start and passing it (plus confirmation) ends the stage at once, even mid-ramp; (3) 25% of stage-2 flights carry a 40%-size boulder (not counted for pace or pass) so route learning starts early; (4) at the deadline (minus 20 min) the trainer stops, re-flies the 5 best-checked champions plus the newest on 1,000 fresh selection flights and picks one; the supervisor then flies both test blocks automatically, also after a goal stop; (5) the local dashboard shows the newest champion flying in its current world. First check after the change: real task 15.5% (new best), stage final world 61%.

title: Training 5x faster: C++ simulator for training flights
text: From gen 267 the training flights of N1 run in C++ (sim/lander_sim.cpp: the same Box2D 2.3.x that box2d-py wraps, plus the NEAT network). Gens 236-251 took 95 s each (32,500 steps/s), gens 252-266 with the fast Python path and a numba network 48 s, and now 18 s (~166,000 steps/s), so ~195 generations an hour instead of 38. Equivalence test on 1,000 analysis seeds in three worlds: bit-identical to a fresh reference env on 3,000 of 3,000 flights, and the same outcome as the reused reference env on 99.7-100% (as often as the reference agrees with itself). Checks, the selection and the goal test still fly the reference Python env; lander/env.py is unchanged. Details on the Speed tab.

title: NEAT itself 4.6x faster between generations
text: After the C++ switch the flights took 18 s per generation but the wall clock 27 s: neat-python spent ~6 s per generation on crossover (its feed-forward cycle check rescans every connection for every inherited gene) and speciation distances while all workers waited. RandomStartGenome now overrides both with the same logic, the same random draws and the same sums: identical populations and species over 3 generations from the N1 checkpoint. From gen 313: ~19 s per generation wall clock (~101 s before today's speed work), ~190 generations an hour. Correction: the earlier note's '~195 an hour' counted flying time only; the wall-clock rate then was ~134.

title: Worker count measured: 8
text: Same 7 generations from the gen-326 checkpoint with 4-8 workers: 22.8, 21.4, 20.2, 19.3 and 18.9 s per generation (7 and 8 alternated three times; 8 won every pair, by ~2%). Going from 4 to 8 workers gains only 17%: 4 physical cores, and hyperthreads add little. N1 continues from gen 327 with 8 workers. The top 10's re-flights now fly the exact fast Python env (the reference's numbers step for step); checks and the champion's selection flights stay in the reference env.

title: Where the champion fails: the wind, not the boulder
text: The user asked whether to restart the curriculum with a small boulder and no wind, then light wind, ramping both. Measured first (experiments/wind_boulder_grid.py, gen-382 champion, 400 analysis flights per cell, C++ sim): calm air lands 86% / 90% (no / full boulder), wind 5: 96% / 85%, wind 10: 94% / 75%, full wind 15 + turbulence 1.5: 73% / 53%. The boulder is already handled in calm and light wind; the bottleneck is strong gusty wind (crashes 15-16%, off-pad 7-9%). So no restart. Proposed instead (waiting for the user): stage 3 ramps wind 10 -> 15 together with the boulder, with ~30% real-task rehearsal. N1 continues unchanged meanwhile.

title: Stage 3 ended at its cap (gen 702) without a pass; stage 4 (real task + hard cases) started
text: The boulder reached full size at gen 578 (paced ramp, mostly at half speed since the champion landed ~60-75% of its flights). Stage 3 needed 85% on the real task and ended at its 400-generation cap instead. Real-task checks (200 fresh flights every 10 gens) averaged 59% over stage 3 and 65% over gens 640-692; the best single check is still 76% at gen 402 (likely partly luck: 200 flights). Stage 4 now flies the real task, with 30% of flights re-flying seeds recent champions failed (hard cases). Still at ~19.5 s per generation. Open question for the user (wind 10->15 together with the boulder) is moot now that stage 3 is over; the hard-case stage is the next lever.

title: Stage 4 plateau: ~66% on the real task after 146 generations of hard cases
text: Gens 702-848 (stage 4: the real task, 32 flights per genome, 30% re-flown hard cases). The 15 real-task checks (200 fresh flights each) average 65.6% landed: 63.8% for gens 702-762, 67.1% for 772-842, best 73.5% at gen 832; the best ever is still 76% at gen 402. Failures on average: crashes ~13%, boulder touches ~10%, off-pad ~8%, timeouts ~3.5%. About 22 s per generation (32 flights instead of 24). At ~160 generations an hour the climb is about 3 points per 100 generations: not enough for 95% by Friday without a change. Candidate levers to discuss with the user: a larger population or more flights per genome (less selection noise), a stronger hard-case share, reward shaping for the crash/off-pad cases, or seeding from the stage-2 wind champion.

title: Stage 4 climbing again: new best 76.5% on the real task (gen 982)
text: Gens 852-982: the real-task checks (200 fresh flights each) average 69.6%, and the last 9 (gens 902-982) 72.1%, against 65.6% for gens 702-842. New best check 76.5% at gen 982 (the old best was 76% at gen 402); 200 flights, so the 95% interval is roughly 70-82%. Failures in the last 9 checks: boulder ~8%, off-pad ~6%, timeouts ~2%, crashes ~12%. ~23 s per generation, 12 species. The 23:40 'plateau' note was early: the climb is ~4-5 points per 100 generations, still short of 95% by Friday at this pace.

title: Stall at ~70%: gens 992-1132 average 69.6% on the real task
text: 15 real-task checks (200 fresh flights each) from gen 992 to 1132 average 69.6% (range 63-76.5%), the same level as gens 852-982 (69.6%); best still 76.5% at gen 982. Since gen ~900 there is no clear trend: a stall of ~230 generations at ~70%. Failures: boulder ~9%, off-pad ~8.5%, timeouts ~3%, crashes ~10%. 23.6 s per generation, 15 species. Stage 4 alone will not reach 95% by Friday; a change needs the user's decision (candidates: more flights per genome, larger hard-case share, reward for the off-pad/boulder failures, bigger population).

title: Correction: no stall; new best 82.5% on the real task (gen 1212)
text: The 01:46 note called a stall at ~70%. The next 14 real-task checks (gens 1142-1272, 200 fresh flights each) average 76.0% (range 67.5-82.5%), against 69.6% for gens 992-1132. New best 82.5% at gen 1212 (95% interval roughly 77-87% on 200 flights). Failures at gens 1202-1272: boulder ~6.5%, off-pad ~5.5%, timeouts ~3.5%, crashes ~6%. 23.6 s per generation, 13 species. Lesson: with 200-flight checks swinging +-5 points, a 'stall' needs far more than 150 generations of evidence; I called a plateau twice too early. At ~6 points per 140 generations, 95% by Friday is still unlikely without a change, but the trend is up.

title: Real task above 80%: checks average 80.3%, new best 85.5% (gen 1652)
text: Gens 1542-1662: 13 real-task checks (200 fresh flights each) average 80.3% (range 68.5-85.5%), up from 75.5% (gens 1412-1532) and 74.3% (1282-1402). New best 85.5% at gen 1652 (95% interval roughly 80-90% on 200 flights). The champion lands 86% of its own training flights. ~25.5 s per generation, 12 species. Pace since gen 1000: about 10 points per 650 generations; 95% by Friday 17:00 leaves ~15,000 generations at 25 s each; reachable only if the climb holds, and it usually slows near the top.

title: New best 87% on the real task (gen 1692); average holds at ~81%
text: Gens 1672-1802: 14 real-task checks (200 fresh flights each) average 80.8% (range 72-87%), level with the previous hour (80.3%). New best 87% at gen 1692 (95% interval roughly 82-91% on 200 flights). ~24.6 s per generation, 14 species.

title: Plateau at ~79-80% since gen 1542 (~690 generations)
text: Hourly averages of the real-task checks (200 fresh flights each, 13-14 checks per hour): gens 1542-1662 80.3%, 1672-1802 80.8%, 1812-1942 78.9%, 1952-2082 78.9%, 2092-2222 79.1%. Best single check 87% (gen 1692). Unlike the earlier false stalls (~150-230 gens), this one spans ~690 generations and 5 hourly windows with no upward trend. ~24 s per generation, 12-16 species. ~4.3 days left; 95% needs a change: candidate levers for the user (more flights per genome to cut selection noise, larger hard-case share, a bigger population, or reward for the remaining failure types), measured on the gen-1692 champion first.

title: New best 88% on the real task (gen 2362); hourly average 81.4%
text: Gens 2232-2372: 15 real-task checks (200 fresh flights each) average 81.4% (range 74.5-88%), the highest hourly average so far, after 78.9-79.1% for the previous three hours. New best 88% at gen 2362 (95% interval roughly 83-92% on 200 flights). The champion lands 91.7% of its own training flights. ~23 s per generation, 13 species. The plateau noted at 09:46 may be ending, but one hour is not enough to tell.

title: Correction: the plateau ended; hourly average 84.8%, new best 90% (gen 2462)
text: Gens 2382-2522: 15 real-task checks (200 fresh flights each) average 84.8% (range 79.5-90%), after 81.4% (2232-2372) and ~79% (1812-2222). New best 90% at gen 2462 (95% interval roughly 85-93% on 200 flights). So the 09:46 plateau note (~690 generations flat) was wrong too: the third early stall call in this run. NEAT's progress here comes in steps after long flat stretches (likely a new structure spreading). ~22.7 s per generation, 13 species. No change to training.

title: Five hours level at ~82% (gens 2532-3302)
text: Hourly averages of the real-task checks (200 fresh flights each): 80.9%, 82.4%, 82.6%, 82.4%, 81.1% for gens 2532-3302 (~770 generations); best still 90% at gen 2462. Not called a stall: the last flat stretch (~690 generations at 79-80%) ended in a climb. Generations got faster (~20 s, 12 species). ~4 days left; the open proposal to measure changes (more flights per genome, larger hard-case share, bigger population) stands.

title: Remeasured: the population lost its best genome; flights 32 -> 64
text: Champions re-flown on the same 1,000 analysis seeds (C++ sim, real task): gen 432 54.4%, 682 65.4%, 1432 78.2%, 1932 81.9%, 2432 85.0%, 2462 (the 90% check) 88.1%, 2932 86.5%, 3182 80.7%, 3352 83.4%, 3402 83.0%. Real progress up to ~gen 2450, then none: the best genome measured is 700-950 generations old and today's champions are ~5 points worse. Cause: every genome's fitness comes from 32 training flights; at ~85% landed one flight count has a standard error of ~6 points, so NEAT cannot rank parents 2-5 points apart and a better genome can lose to a lucky worse one. Change (live, override.json, no restart): 64 flights per genome from the next generation (hard cases stay 30%). Variance halves (standard error ~4.5 points); generations take ~2x longer (~9,000 left before Friday instead of ~17,000). The final pick still re-flies the best-checked champions (gen 2462 among them) on 1,000 fresh flights, so the 88% genome is not lost for the deadline.

title: After 64 flights: checks average 87.9%, new best 91.5% (gen 3462)
text: Twelve real-task checks (200 fresh flights each) since the switch to 64 flights per genome at gen 3431 average 87.9% (85-91.5%), against 81.1% in the hour before. New best check 91.5% at gen 3462 (old 90% at gen 2462). Early: one hour, and the best of many checks is flattered (winner's curse); the trend needs a few more hours and a 1,000-flight remeasure. ~37 s per generation (was ~20 s with 32 flights), 16 species.

title: Best measured: gen 3582 lands 90.1% on 1,000 flights
text: New script experiments/remeasure.py flies champions on the same 1,000 unseen analysis seeds (real task, C++ sim) and writes results/baseline_N1_g*.json for the Log page's table. Gen 2462 88.1% (crash 5.7, boulder 4.0), gen 2932 86.5%, gen 3462 (the 91.5% check) 87.3%, gen 3582 90.1% (95% interval ~88.1-91.8; crash 4.9, boulder 4.5, off-pad 0.1, timeout 0.4). 150 generations after the switch to 64 flights the population holds a genome 2 points better than its old best: the first fair evidence the change works. 95% needs about half of the remaining crashes and boulder touches gone.

title: Bug fixed: "Watch it think" showed every node at zero
text: Since the numba speed-up (2026-11-01) the network computes its action in a compiled kernel that keeps node values in its own buffer; the Model page recorder still read the old numpy buffer, which stayed all zero, so the drawing never lit up. Fixed with NeatJsonNet.node_values() and a test (tests/test_core.py::test_node_values_are_the_last_call_s). Training was not affected: only the drawing read the stale buffer.

title: New best check 94% (gen 3712); best measured 91.3% on 1,000 flights
text: Real-task checks for gens 3642-3722 average 89.8% (9 checks, 86.5-94%), up from 88.1% and 87.9% in the two hours before and 81.1% before the switch to 64 flights. New best checks 93% (gen 3662) and 94% (gen 3712). On the same 1,000 unseen flights: gen 3662 91.1% (crash 5.2, boulder 2.6), gen 3712 91.3% (95% interval ~89.4-92.9; crash 3.8, boulder 3.8, off-pad 0.7, timeout 0.4), newest gen 3722 90.1%. The 94% check is ~3 points of luck on top of a ~91% pilot (winner's curse). Steady gain: best measured 88.1 -> 90.1 -> 91.3% in ~280 generations at 64 flights. ~40 s per generation, 16 species.

title: Hourly average 91.2%; best measured 93.0% (gen 3832)
text: Ten real-task checks for gens 3822-3912 average 91.2% (87-92.5%), the best hour so far (previous hours 88.7%, 89.8%, 88.1%). On the same 1,000 unseen flights: gen 3832 93.0% (95% interval ~91.3-94.4; crash 2.3, boulder 3.1, off-pad 1.0, timeout 0.6), gen 3872 91.8%, gen 3912 92.1%. Best measured since the switch to 64 flights at gen 3431: 88.1 -> 90.1 -> 91.3 -> 93.0% in ~400 generations. 95% needs ~2 of the remaining 7 failures per 100 gone. ~36 s per generation, 12 species.

title: Drift again at ~90%: flights 64 -> 128, and the deadline pick now includes the best measured
text: Hourly check averages for gens 3822-4285: 91.2, 89.1, 91.1, 89.6, 88.8% (level ~90% for ~450 generations). Champions re-flown on the same 1,000 unseen flights: gen 3832 93.0%, 3882 92.4%, 3912 92.1%, 3982 89.0%, 4082 91.3%, 4182 88.0%, 4282 86.3%: the population has drifted down from its best again, with boulder touches up from 3.1% to 6.4%. Same cause as at gen 3431, one level higher: near 90% a 64-flight fitness has a ~3.7-point standard error and the gains left are 1-3 points. Change at gen 4300 (graceful stop, checkpoint, restart): 128 flights per genome (~2.6-point error, ~75 s per generation, ~4,000 generations to the deadline). Bug fixed in the same restart: the deadline pick re-flew only the 5 best 200-flight checks plus the newest champion, so the best measured pilot (gen 3832, 93.0%; its check of 92% was never a best) would have been left out; the 5 best 1,000-flight measurements (results/baseline_N1_g*.json) now join the candidates. Tests: 34 passed.

title: First 95% check (gen 4402); 1,000 fresh flights say 92.4%
text: Gen 4402 landed 95.0% of its 200-flight real-task check, the first check at the goal. The run then re-flew it on 1,000 fresh selection flights, as designed: 92.4% (crash 3.7, boulder 3.5, timeout 0.4, off-pad 0.0), so no goal candidate. On the same 1,000 analysis flights as the other champions: 92.2%. Winner's curse in action: the best of many noisy checks overstates by ~2.6 points here. Hourly check average for gens 4402-4452: 92.8% (91.5-95%, 6 checks), the best hour so far; 128 flights per genome since gen 4302 average 91.6% over 16 checks. Best measured still gen 3832 (93.0%). ~58 s per generation, 13 species.

title: 128 flights: no drift, but no gain yet (gens 4302-4618)
text: Hourly check averages since 128 flights: 91.0, 90.7, 92.8, 90.5, 89.7, 89.7%. On the same 1,000 unseen flights: gen 4372 90.5%, 4402 92.2%, 4432 90.9%, 4492 90.8%, 4552 89.8%, 4612 91.0%. The slide seen at 64 flights (93 -> 86%) has stopped, but the population sits ~2 points below its best measured pilot (gen 3832, 93.0%) after ~320 generations (~6 h at ~65 s each). Not called a stall yet. Next lever if no gain in a few hours: put copies of the best measured pilots back into the population. ~3.3 days left.

title: Best measured pilots put back into the population (gen 4681)
text: At 128 flights the population held ~90.5% on 1,000 flights for ~380 generations (hourly checks 91.0, 90.7, 92.8, 90.5, 89.7, 89.7, 91.0%) but never regained the pilots lost earlier to 64-flight noise. New override "inject" (evo/train.py, lander/neatnet.py from_json; exact round trip on 2,000 inputs, test, dry run on the gen-4670 checkpoint): the three best measured pilots (gen 3832 93.0%, 3882 92.4%, 4402 92.2%) each replace 5 random genomes (1 exact copy, 4 mutated once), then the population is re-speciated (dry run: 13 -> 16 species). 15 of 300 genomes; they must still win on fitness. Clean restart at gen 4680; tests 35 passed. Expect: the copies take over within ~50-100 generations if they really are better at 128 flights, then evolution continues from ~93%.

title: Injected pilots took over within ~40 generations
text: Every champion since gen 4712 shares 87-98% of its connections with one of the injected pilots (gen 3832/3882 line or gen 4402 line; ~45% with the other line), so the copies won on fitness at 128 flights. On the same 1,000 unseen flights: gen 4722 93.0%, gen 4742 92.6%, gen 4762 89.0% (timeouts 2.3%). Back at the best level, not above it yet. Hourly checks: 90.7% (gens 4682-4712), 89.3% (4722-4762). ~74 s per generation, 11 species.

title: Best hour of checks (93.9%), but 1,000 flights say ~90.5%
text: Four real-task checks for gens 4822-4852: 94.5, 94.5, 93, 93.5% (average 93.9%, the best hour so far). The same four champions on the same 1,000 unseen flights: 92.0, 89.4, 90.6, 90.8% (average 90.7%). Four 200-flight checks can all run high together by luck (a 3-point gap here); judge on the 1,000-flight measure. Best measured still 93.0% (gens 3832 and 4722). ~73 s per generation, 12 species, ~3 days 3 h left.

title: Training paused by the user (gen 4895)
text: Clean stop at gen 4895 (checkpoint saved, 128 flights per genome, override state kept). Resume with the same supervise command; nothing is lost except time to the deadline (Fri 6 Nov 17:00).
